claims.text: Adding a modest volume fraction of h-BN nanoparticles to CoCrFeNi will enable in-situ formation of a continuous lubricious tribolayer during sliding.
The h-BN-derived tribolayer will remain effective from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C.
The h-BN-modified alloy will have a lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the stated temperature range.
The h-BN-modified alloy will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the stated temperature range.
The incorporated h-BN nanoparticles will be evenly dispersed in the CoCrFeNi matrix.
Sliding will cause the dispersed h-BN nanoparticles to participate in tribolayer formation at the wear interface.
The layered structure of h-BN will produce a self-adaptive tribolayer under sliding.
The h-BN-derived tribolayer will significantly reduce contact shear stress.
The tribolayer will mitigate direct metal-to-metal contact.
The tribolayer will favor controlled oxide formation.
Reduced contact shear stress and metal-to-metal contact will lower friction.
Tribolayer formation and controlled oxidation will reduce wear.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi typically exhibits increased friction at elevated temperatures.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi typically exhibits increased wear at elevated temperatures.
The elevated-temperature degradation of unmodified CoCrFeNi is caused by less effective oxide or hardening mechanisms.
The proposed performance advantage is expected in ambient air under loads and sliding speeds that do not cause catastrophic deformation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts lower friction and wear throughout the full 25–800 °C range, but the falsification rule only requires a statistically significant benefit over at least 50% of the tested range. Thus, a result failing over nearly half of the range could avoid falsification despite contradicting the stated full-range prediction.
